title: Ease may travel alongside hardship, not only after

points.label: What research comes close
points.text: Exegetes read the pair grammatically: **al-ʿusr** has the article, so verse 6 repeats the **same hardship**; **yusr** is indefinite, so a second, different ease. Hence the saying, reported via al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī from Muhammad: “**one hardship cannot overcome two eases**.”

points.label: One possible reading
points.text: “With” places ease **inside the same moment** as hardship, not at its end. The chest is opened and the burden lifted **while** the mission is still hard, and verse 7 sends the freed Prophet straight back to toil. Ease accompanies struggle rather than replacing it.

bottom_text: The strongest counter-view: Qur’an 65:7 says God brings ease “after hardship” (baʿda ʿusrin), so maʿa may simply promise ease soon and surely, not at the same time.
